interest: Shows 1941 scramble by Japanese banks to move assets before the freeze, and 1944 planning for Allied military yen.
overview: This file comprises State Department memoranda, inter-agency conference minutes, FBI intelligence bulletins, diplomatic cross-reference sheets, and corporate correspondence spanning June 1941 to March 1944 under decimal file 894.516 (Japanese banking, credits, and public securities). The pre-Pearl Harbor documentation (June–October 1941) details the acute financial friction and regulatory fallout caused by the July 1941 executive order freezing Japanese assets in the United States, including pre-freeze runs and large cash withdrawals in Honolulu, covert attempts by the Yokohama Specie Bank in San Francisco to evacuate $5,000,000 in bonds and institutional records aboard the S.S. Tatuta Maru, corporate inquiries regarding the status of the National City Bank branch in Tokyo, and high-level State-Treasury deliberations over the impending insolvency of the Yokohama Specie Bank's New York agency due to halted bilateral trade, unliquidated silk acceptances, and obligations to service Japanese sovereign and corporate debt. The wartime records (1942–1944) shift to British intelligence monitoring Japanese capital movements in Latin America and currency exploitation in the occupied Netherlands East Indies, culminating in detailed inter-divisional planning for the design, denominations, and inflationary safeguards of Allied Military Yen ('Military Government Currency') for the occupation of Japanese territories.

subfiles.about: Internal State Department memorandum analyzing the dwindling dollar liquidity of the Yokohama Specie Bank's New York agency and outlining potential policy remedies.
subfiles.from: George F. Luthringer and James (Division of Far Eastern Affairs / Office of Economic Adviser, Department of State)
subfiles.summary: Memo reviews the Yokohama Specie Bank New York agency's dollar depletion after the freezing order, weighing options like accepting Japanese gold shipments or Federal Loan Agency purchase of blocked silk bills, and recommends backing a New York banking plan ahead of a Treasury Policy Committee meeting.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Division of Far Eastern Affairs to Assistant Secretary Acheson on the Financial Position of the Yokohama Specie Bank New York Agency

subfiles.about: Record of an inter-agency conference at the Treasury Department reviewing regulatory options and creditor protection concerning the Yokohama Specie Bank in New York.
subfiles.from: Inter-agency Conference Participants (Treasury, State, Federal Reserve Bank of New York, New York State Banking Department, National Bank Examiner)
subfiles.summary: Conference minutes: officials found the Yokohama Specie Bank's New York branch held $8.3 million cash against $9.2 million liabilities plus $19 million doubtful silk receivables; White proposed license monitoring, an escrow account, or forced liquidation, while considering transfers from South America, Hawaii, or Japan.
subfiles.title: Conference Memorandum with Respect to New York Branch of the Yokohama Specie Bank

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing a telegram regarding substantial fund payments from the Java Bank to the Yokohama Specie Bank in New York.
subfiles.summary: Indexes a telegram from Batavia reporting large Java Bank remittances to the Yokohama Specie Bank's New York agency, representing Japan's trade balance in the Netherlands East Indies.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Telegram No. 60 from Batavia Concerning Java Bank Remittances to Yokohama Specie Bank

subfiles.about: Corporate inquiry regarding whether Japanese retaliatory freezing decrees affected the National City Bank branch in Tokyo and disrupted company finances.
subfiles.from: F. S. Thomas (Westinghouse Air Brake Company, Wilmerding, Pa.)
subfiles.summary: A Westinghouse Air Brake executive asks about the National City Bank's Tokyo branch status under Japan's retaliatory freezing orders, noting mail contact with its Tokyo office had been cut for over two months.
subfiles.title: Letter from Westinghouse Air Brake Company Inquiring About the Status of National City Bank in Tokyo

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing Westinghouse Air Brake Company's letter under frozen credits classification.
subfiles.from: F. S. Thomas (Westinghouse Air Brake Company)
subfiles.summary: Indexes Westinghouse Air Brake's August 1941 letter on National City Bank's Tokyo branch under Japanese freezing regulations, filed at 840.51.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Westinghouse Air Brake Company Letter on National City Bank in Tokyo

subfiles.about: State Department reply advising Westinghouse Air Brake Company to contact the New York headquarters of National City Bank for operational details on Tokyo.
subfiles.from: Herbert Feis (Adviser on International Economic Affairs, Department of State)
subfiles.summary: Feis tells Westinghouse Air Brake that National City Bank of New York is kept current on its Tokyo branch's status and suggests contacting the bank's headquarters directly.
subfiles.title: Letter from Herbert Feis to Westinghouse Air Brake Company Regarding National City Bank in Tokyo
subfiles.to: F. S. Thomas (Westinghouse Air Brake Company)

subfiles.about: Confidential intelligence report detailing attempts by the Yokohama Specie Bank's San Francisco branch to evacuate $5,000,000 in bonds and bank records on the S.S. Tatuta Maru.
subfiles.from: Frederick B. Lyon (Division of Foreign Activity Correlation, Department of State)
subfiles.summary: Lyon warns officials that Yokohama Specie Bank's San Francisco manager arranged an armored-car transfer of $5,000,000 in bonds to the S.S. Tatuta Maru and hired a company to ship records to Japan, seeking FBI countermeasure instructions.
subfiles.title: Confidential Memorandum from Frederick B. Lyon Concerning Japanese Attempts to Transfer Bonds and Bank Records
subfiles.to: Sumner Welles, Adolf A. Berle, Jr., and Stanley K. Hornbeck

subfiles.about: Intelligence report on exceptional pre-freezing cash withdrawals by Japanese banks from the Bank of Hawaii in Honolulu.
subfiles.from: Frederick B. Lyon (Division of Foreign Activity Correlation, Department of State)
subfiles.summary: Lyon relays FBI Honolulu intelligence that the Yokohama Specie Bank withdrew $200,000 and Sumitomo Bank $100,000 from the Bank of Hawaii just before Roosevelt's freezing announcement, anticipating depositor runs.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Frederick B. Lyon on Pre-Freezing Cash Withdrawals in Honolulu
subfiles.to: Sumner Welles, Stanley K. Hornbeck, Maxwell M. Hamilton, and Herbert Feis

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing British intelligence on the transfer of Japanese Mitsui Bank funds from Uruguay to Peru.
subfiles.summary: Indexes British information on Mitsui Bank funds transferred from Montevideo to a Lima bank, filed at 865.516/212.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: British Information on Transfer of Mitsui Bank Funds from Montevideo to Lima

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing a British economic warfare despatch on Japanese currency devaluation in the occupied Dutch East Indies.
subfiles.summary: Indexes a British despatch analyzing currency devaluation and Japanese military banking policy in the occupied Netherlands East Indies.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: British Despatch on Devaluation of Dutch East Indies Currency
subfiles.to: Department of State / British Foreign Office

subfiles.about: Inter-divisional policy memorandum outlining design guidelines, linguistic specifications, and denomination choices for Allied Military Yen currency.
subfiles.from: Abbot Low Moffat (Division of Liberated Areas, Department of State)
subfiles.summary: Moffat records State's design plan for Allied military yen: bamboo over cherry-blossom motifs, bilingual English-kanji text, and heavy small-denomination printing to avoid wage inflation seen in occupied Italy.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Abbot Low Moffat Concerning Basic Designs and Denominations for Military Yen
subfiles.to: Jacques J. Reinstein (Division of Liberated Areas, Department of State)
